items.proposedAnswer: Tropical rainforest is found in the Amazon basin, tundra in the Arctic regions, and desert vegetation in the Sahara.

items.q: How can large-scale deforestation affect the water cycle and local climate?
items.proposedAnswer: Fewer trees mean less transpiration and less moisture in the air, which can reduce rainfall locally. Without roots to hold soil, runoff and soil erosion increase and groundwater recharge may fall.

items.q: State two differences between Himalayan rivers and peninsular rivers.
items.proposedAnswer: Himalayan rivers are perennial as they are fed by snow and rain, while peninsular rivers are mostly seasonal. Himalayan rivers have long courses and large basins, while peninsular rivers are shorter and flow through older, stable land.

items.q: State two causes and two effects of drought in India.
items.proposedAnswer: Causes include failure or delay of the monsoon and long gaps in rainfall. Effects include crop failure, shortage of drinking water and fodder, and loss of rural income.

items.q: What is meant by a parliamentary system of government?
items.proposedAnswer: In a parliamentary system the executive is drawn from the legislature and is answerable to it. The head of State is nominal, while real power lies with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers who must keep the confidence of the House.
keyPoints: nominal head of State and real head of government

items.q: Why must certain parts of the Constitution be amended only with the consent of the States?
items.proposedAnswer: Matters that affect the federal structure, such as the distribution of powers between the Union and the States, concern both levels. Requiring State consent, along with a special majority in Parliament, prevents the Centre from changing them alone.
keyPoints: federal matters concern both Centre and States

items.proposedAnswer: A citizen has equal rights, takes part in choosing the government and can question it, while a subject owes obedience to a ruler and has no equal political rights.

items.q: Why is the freedom of the press important in a democracy?
items.proposedAnswer: A free press informs citizens about the working of the government and public issues, which helps them take part and vote wisely. It also exposes wrongdoing, which makes those in power accountable.

items.q: State two functions of the judiciary.
items.proposedAnswer: The judiciary settles disputes between citizens, and between citizens and the government, by interpreting and applying the law. It also protects the Fundamental Rights and can examine whether laws follow the Constitution.

items.q: Why is it important that the Election Commission works independently?
items.proposedAnswer: An independent Commission can conduct elections fairly and without pressure from the government in power. This keeps voters' confidence in the result and the democratic process.
